question: According to the business newspaper De Tijd, the Belgian Government intends to introduce tolls on the road network via a digital tax disk from 1 May 2027.1 Belgian citizens will be compensated through a reduction in road tax, meaning that, in reality, only foreign drivers will be affected by this proposal. In 2017, Dutch Minister Van Nieuwenhuizen took the matter to the Court of Justice of the European Union to challenge similar discriminatory toll plans by Germany.2 In view of this: 1.
What is the Commission’s position on this proposal by the Belgian Government?
Does the Commission consider this proposal to be compatible with the European single market?

Should this plan be implemented, does the Commission intend to bring a case before the Court of Justice of the European Union on behalf of the Member States and/or to take measures against the Belgian Government to have this plan annulled?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.9.2026) 1 and 2. Tolls and user charges (the latter also commonly known as ‘vignettes’) are regulated in the EU under Directive 1999/62/EC on the charging of vehicles for the use of road infrastructures1. The Belgian government intends to levy a new user charge on light-duty vehicles, including passenger cars, starting next year.

While Article 7h of the Directive requires Member States to notify in advance new tolls for heavy-duty vehicles, this notification requirement does not apply to the present case as light-duty vehicles are not in scope of this notification requirement. Directive 1999/62/EC does not prevent by itself reforms of other national legislation at the same time as the implementation of a new road charge.
However, all national legislation must comply with the EU treaties, including Article 18 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union on non-discrimination on grounds of nationality. 3.

The Commission may assess the compliance of the new charging system with EU law and, should a breach of EU law be identified, it may initiate the necessary steps to ensure that it complies with EU law, including with the principle of non-discrimination.
